title: How To Love Being A Teacher
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Reflecting on 25 years in the classroom and seven years running SCM, Linsin observes that teaching has grown harder and more stressful, yet a small group of teachers has figured out how to eliminate the pressure and genuinely enjoy the job. He announces his forthcoming book, The Happy Teacher Habits, describing it as the culmination of his career-long search for the single most effective and fulfilling teaching approach, drawing on research into learning, happiness, motivation, and performance as well as lessons from fields like music, sports, and comedy. He explains the book distills these findings into eleven applicable habits meant to simplify and de-stress a teaching career, with an emphasis on showing readers exactly why each strategy works rather than simply asserting it. The article functions as both a personal reflection and a book announcement, with the release date set for the following Tuesday.

quotes: More is being asked of us now than at any time in my 25 years of teaching. Stress is at an all-time high.
And yet, there is a small band of teachers who have figured out how to fight back.
They’ve figured out how to love being a teacher. (And not just try to convince themselves they do.)

The book is a culmination of my career-long quest for the single most effective and fulfilling teaching approach in existence—and not just in the classroom, but from the moment you arrive on campus until you leave for the day.
I’ve taken the traits, qualities, and practices of the happiest and most effective teachers on Earth and condensed them into 11 habits any teacher can apply and experience dramatic results.
It was important to me not just to tell you that a particular method or strategy is effective, but show you exactly why it’s effective and how you can apply it in your own classroom.
